proposals.title: Branded numeric types and explicit-mode division helper (ADR-003 + ADR-004)
proposals.why_now: Every subsequent FASE-1 deliverable — ledger entries, price queries, order execution, RNG coordinates, and the tick loop — requires the primitive type vocabulary defined by ADR-003 and ADR-004. Money, Quantity, Price, Rate as bigint branded types and Tick as a safe-integer nominal type are the foundational vocabulary that prevents silent misuse of arithmetic values. ADR-004's division helper with explicit rounding mode and residue return is required before any economic arithmetic code can exist. ADR-004 has a DEFINIR item — the technical enforcement mechanism — that must be specified in an ADR before implementation begins. Without these types the ledger, the price generator, the RNG parameter encoding, and the tick loop cannot be correctly typed. This work is independent of everything and unblocks the longest blocking chain in FASE-1.

proposals.title: StateHash and SaveHash: ADR and implementation in packages/core
proposals.why_now: The CanonicalEncoder (ADR-009) is now accepted. StateHash is the immediate next deliverable it enables. INV-01 (replay produces identical StateHash at every tick), INV-22 (logically equal states produce equal canonical bytes; finalTick excluded from StateHash), the FASE-1 CI gate (replay of three reference games comparing StateHash by tick), and tools/replay (first divergent-tick comparison) all require StateHash and SaveHash to exist. The spec is precise about what enters each hash: StateHash explicitly excludes finalTick, narrative text, cached projections, and UI data; SaveHash includes masterSeed, the full action log, finalTick, specVersion, rulesetVersion, and encodingVersion. These must be separate types that cannot be confused at the type level. An ADR must specify which hash primitive is applied to canonical bytes — this is distinct from the ADR-002 RNG hash and requires its own specification.

proposals.title: Positional RNG with hash primitive ADR and rand() implementation in packages/core (ADR-002)
proposals.why_now: The price generator (trendLayer, idiosyncraticNoise, regimeAmplitude, marketFactor), macro event scheduler, bot policy derivation, venue liquidity, and NPC tip truth all consume rand(masterSeed, namespace, ...coordinates). None of them can be implemented until rand() exists. ADR-002 designates the hash primitive as DEFINIR with two hard constraints: it must be specified bit-by-bit in an ADR, and it cannot be the native language hash function. The spec recommends SplitMix64 over FNV-1a. INV-02 (price at tick T queried directly equals tick-by-tick arrival) and INV-03 (player actions do not alter worldPrice series) are untestable until rand() is available. All namespace isolation guarantees must be verified by test. This is an immediate unblock for packages/world and for the FASE-1 price generator with two assets.

proposals.title: Electron security scaffolding, simulation worker IPC, and minimum installer (INV-29 + FASE-1)
proposals.why_now: FASE-1 acceptance explicitly requires a minimum installer for Windows and Linux produced by CI and the simulation already running in a dedicated worker outside the rendering thread with a typed message contract. §14.6 warns that discovering packaging, ABI, and path issues at the end of the project is unrecoverable — a window that opens but shows little in FASE-1 is more valuable than a perfect installer in FASE-7. INV-29 (contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, sandbox:true) is a FASE-1 acceptance criterion and is verified in the CI gate. All four app stub directories exist but contain only empty exports. This work is fully independent of all domain code and can proceed while branded types and RNG are being built. Each cycle without this work increases the probability of discovering a cross-platform packaging failure too late to fix it.

proposals.title: Multi-commodity double-entry ledger foundation in packages/domain (INV-04 through INV-07)
proposals.why_now: The ledger is the invariant anchor of the entire economic simulation. INV-04 (every transaction sums to zero per commodity), INV-05 (sum of all BRL accounts is zero every tick), INV-06 (sum of all asset quantity accounts is zero every tick), and INV-07 (rounding residue in world:rounding_residue fully explains every truncation) are all FASE-1 acceptance criteria that require the ledger to exist. No order execution, no position tracking, no margin calculation, and no tick loop can be implemented without a working ledger. The ledger has no dependency on the price generator or the RNG — it depends only on the branded types from IDEA-001. This is the first domain deliverable that should follow branded type acceptance and represents the economic substrate for all gameplay.

repository_assessment.current_state: Monorepo scaffold and CI pipeline are operational. packages/core exports a fully implemented CanonicalEncoder (ADR-009 accepted as TASK-0009; docs/decisions/0009-canonical-encoding.md present). All other packages (world, domain, application, narrative, contracts, adapters, ui) export only empty stubs. No ADRs exist for ADR-002, ADR-003, or ADR-004. No branded types, no positional RNG, no StateHash/SaveHash, no ledger, no price generator, no tick loop, no save/load, no replay CLI, no bench calibration, and no Electron scaffold beyond empty stubs. Zero FASE-1 acceptance criteria are currently green beyond the CanonicalEncoder.
repository_assessment.highest_priority_gap: No branded numeric types (Money, Quantity, Price, Rate, Tick) exist in packages/core and ADR-004 (division rounding enforcement) has not been written. These are the foundational vocabulary that blocks the ledger, price generator, RNG coordinate encoding, tick loop, and order execution — the entire economic simulation cannot be correctly typed without them.

warnings: The hash primitive used inside rand() (ADR-002) and the hash primitive applied to canonical bytes for StateHash/SaveHash are two separate DEFINIR items requiring two separate ADRs with bit-by-bit specifications. They must not share an implementation or be conflated in authorship.

ADR-004 technical enforcement mechanism is DEFINIR. Any division or arithmetic code written before the enforcement ADR is committed cannot satisfy the compile-time or lint-time guarantee the spec requires. The ADR must be written before the first division helper line of code exists.

tools/bench calibration ratios must be frozen in FASE-1 (§18 baseline protocol). These ratios cannot be frozen until packages/core and packages/world are implemented. The bench tool currently exists only as an empty stub; deferring calibration past FASE-1 acceptance violates §15 and §18.

The transcendental-function prohibition in §13 combined with the price generator requirement for logarithmic construction (logPrice) creates an implementation constraint: fixed-point or lookup-table implementations of log and exp must be specified before packages/world arithmetic is written. This approach should be captured in an ADR before packages/world implementation begins.
